Shipping Exception Workflow Procedure

Purpose
This procedure defines the shipping exception workflow for orders affected by shipping delays, carrier scans that stop updating, address issues, damage in transit, or delivery exceptions. Fast and accurate handling reduces customer contacts, protects carrier claim recovery, and keeps fulfillment teams aligned with support operations.

Exception Types
Common shipping exceptions include label created with no carrier acceptance, in-transit delay beyond the service commitment, attempted delivery due to address problem, package marked delivered but not received, damaged parcel, and returned-to-sender. Each exception type may require different ownership between Fulfillment, Customer Support, Carrier Relations, and Finance.

Monitoring and Intake
Shipping exceptions may be identified through carrier dashboards, automated alerts, warehouse reports, or customer contacts. The first owner opening the case must validate the tracking number, shipping method, order value, promised delivery date, and exception code. If multiple orders are impacted by the same carrier or warehouse issue, the shift lead should open a parent incident and link related cases.

Resolution Steps
Step one: verify the most recent carrier event and compare it with the order promise date and applicable service-level buffer. Step two: determine whether the package is likely still moving, requires customer action, or should be treated as lost or undeliverable. Step three: contact the carrier or open a trace when required by carrier rules. Step four: choose the customer solution, which may include wait-and-monitor, address correction, replacement shipment, refund, or claim filing. Step five: document all actions and set a follow-up date in the case system.

Customer Communication Rules
Customers should receive proactive communication when the company becomes aware of a material delay that is likely to affect the promised delivery date. Messages must state what happened, what action is being taken, and when the next update will be sent. Agents should avoid blaming the carrier without evidence and should not promise a refund or replacement before confirming policy eligibility.

Operational Thresholds
Orders above $250, temperature-sensitive goods, subscription replenishments, and replacement shipments receive priority review. Orders with potential fraud indicators should not be automatically reshipped. Returned-to-sender packages caused by verified warehouse labeling errors may be reshipped without additional customer charge once the root cause is documented.

Claims and Internal Follow-Up
Carrier claims must be filed within the service-specific deadline and include photos, tracking evidence, and proof of value where required. Repeated carrier failures by lane, service level, or fulfillment center are reviewed weekly by Fulfillment leadership. If the same root cause affects five or more orders in a 24-hour period, Operations opens a corrective action item with clear owners and due dates.

Documentation Standards
Every shipping exception case must include tracking status, exception type, customer impact, next follow-up date, and final resolution. Accurate coding is mandatory because exception data is used for carrier performance reviews and customer experience analysis.

Shift Handoff
Open exception cases must be included in the next shift handoff whenever follow-up is pending with a carrier, warehouse, or customer. The handoff note should state the last action taken, the next due time, and any risk of missed delivery promise.
